title: The Crying God of Japan
topic: In a long-forgotten village, a deity weeps for eternity. Its tears have the power to heal, but at a terrible cost. The locals call it the Namahage.

title: The Curse of Tezcatlipoca
topic: Meet Tezcatlipoca, Aztec god of night. He's often depicted as a giant jaguar. His power is immense, controlling fate. He tricks and punishes, mercilessly. One myth says he destroyed a city. The city's people were never seen again. Want to know more about Tezcatlipoca? Follow for more mythological tales.

title: The Nuckelnave: Scotland's Deadliest Monster
topic: A creature so horrifying, the sea was its only cage. Break it loose, and all land dies. This is the Nuckelnave. A nightmare from Orkney Island folklore, off Scotland's northern coast. It has no legs. Its green, rotting flesh peels away from the bone. Ribs exposed like a cage. Its face hangs from its chest like a cracked bell. title: The Snow Father Who Kidnapped Children
topic: Deep in the Arctic, the Sámi people tell of Muohta-Áhčči, the Snow Father. He lives inside a frozen mountain and steals young girls to be his wives. The girls are taken into his icy hall, where they never see sunlight again. They are kept there by the endless winter magic that holds the mountain shut. But the Snow Father has a daughter. title: The Georgian Titan Who Stole Fire
topic: Amirani was a giant man, a Titan who lived in ancient Georgia. He loved his people deeply. The sky gods hoarded fire and kept it locked away from humans. Amirani refused to let his people freeze. He climbed Mount Kazbek and wrestled the fire from the gods' vault. He snatched the flames and brought them down. The gods were furious. title: The Water Demon That Haunted Russian Mills
topic: Every night, a man named Levko heard wet footsteps behind the mill walls. Something was trying to get in. He had no idea it was already inside. The mill stood on a swollen river in rural Ukraine. The water was always murky and smelled of rot. Locals refused to walk near it after sunset. title: The Spirit Who Stole Children From The Ice
topic: A mother's cry echoed across the frozen tundra of Nunavut. Her seven-year-old daughter had vanished from their igloo overnight. The Inuit elders told her of the Qalupalik. A pale sea spirit with green hair who lived beneath the ice. She knew the story. The Qalupalik lured children close with a song that sounded like a mother calling their name. title: The Bunyip: Australia's Ancient Water Beast
topic: A low groan echoes through the Australian swamp at dusk. No bird makes that sound. No animal does. The Aboriginal elders say it is the Bunyip. The Bunyip is one of the oldest living stories in the world. Some traditions describe it as a bear-like creature. Others say it has a horse's head and elephant's trunk. title: The Moon the Dog Shattered
topic: Long ago, the sky held only one perfect moon. It hung in the darkness, full and bright. But a celestial dog howled at it. Its bark rang across the heavens. The moon cracked into pieces. Each fragment became a star. That is why the sky shines with countless lights tonight. Nomads warned their children: do not bark at the moon. It remembers. The myth still warns today.

title: The Bird That Guided a Nation
topic: In ancient times, sky god Ülken sent a golden bird to find a homeland. The Magyars were wandering. The bird circled the Carpathian Basin, then perched on a rock peak. Following its call, the tribal leaders settled there. They built a kingdom. But greed arose. Brothers fought over the land. The bird returned, its golden feathers glowing. title: The Dragon Who Ate a Kingdom
topic: Beneath Wawel Castle in Kraków lived a dragon that demanded six sheep daily. When the king refused, it threatened the city. Panic spread through Kraków. The royal blacksmiths failed. Everyone was helpless. A cobbler's son named Skuba volunteered. He had a plan: hide sulfur inside a sheep. The dragon devoured it and drank desperately. title: The Firefly That Steals Hearts
topic: In Togo, the Adze hides as a firefly by day. At night, it wears a human face and visits families. It slips into sleeping children through the ear. The children waste away with no known illness. A shaman must find the glowing firefly first. Burning it destroys the spirit completely. The children recover, and the village is safe.

title: The Sea Mother's Wrath
topic: Sedna was a woman who married a dog. Her father discovered the truth and rowed away. She clung to the kayak as he pushed her off. She sank to the ocean floor and grabbed the rocks. Her fingers stretched into seals, whales, and fish. She became goddess Sedna, mother of all sea life. Inuit hunters fear her, for she controls every creature below.

title: The Sisters Who Became Rivers
topic: In Arnhem Land, two sisters carried sacred fire across the desert. They walked for days, pursued by warriors seeking the flames. Catching crocodiles blocking their path, they transformed into great rainbow serpents. Their winding bodies carved deep channels across the land.
